scope: Purposive source review of sixteen living-town or modern-settlement candidates in five present countries, with two abandoned Indus contrasts. Not an exhaustive oldest-town ranking.
date_convention: Positive BCE numbers; earliest >= latest. A phase range is not a confidence interval for a founding date. CE and uncalibrated results remain labelled in separate fields.
coordinate_scope: All 18 main pins are approximate regional index points with 5 km stated precision; inspect the spatial relation before using them as evidence locations.

records.name: Peshawar

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living city in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa; pin indexes the Gor Khatri area.

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Institutional synthesis reports about 2300 years of stratified occupation at Gor Khatri; approximate onset, not a calibrated founding interval.

records.urban_foundation: Early urban onset beyond this complex is not independently fixed by the reviewed source.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Gor Khatri lies within the living walled city; evidence is a bounded excavated complex.
known_hiatuses: No hiatus is reported by the tentative-list synthesis; full layer-by-layer proof to the present was not audited.
records.summary: Gor Khatri preserves a long urban sequence inside Peshawar. The reported sequence begins over a millennium after the Late Harappan comparison interval.
gaps: Obtain Durrani and Ali excavation reports and their dated layer tables.
An age claim for the wider Peshawar valley cannot supply an earlier date for this urban locus.

records.name: Multan

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living city and municipal centre in Punjab.

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Reviewed official fort account and regional survey research do not provide a secure Bronze Age-to-modern sequence beneath the city.

records.urban_foundation: Historical city; no numerical urban founding date adopted.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: The living city and fort are distinct from early sites elsewhere in Multan district and the alluvial region.
known_hiatuses: City-wide sequence and hiatuses are unresolved in the searched primary evidence.
records.summary: Multan is a living historic city. A date for a nearby Harappan mound cannot date its fort or establish uninterrupted occupation beneath the present city.
gaps: Acquire and reassess old fort excavation records, sample contexts and chronological methods.
Locate a modern stratigraphic sequence through the second millennium BCE and later periods.
This review leaves the city's earliest archaeological occupation unknown.

records.name: Taxila

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living modern Taxila in Punjab beside several protected archaeological settlements.

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: UNESCO synthesis dates the earliest historic city, Bhir; earlier Saraikala is a separate mound.

earlier_regional_evidence.date_label: Neolithic, Bronze Age and Iron Age
earlier_regional_evidence.relationship: Separate early settlement in the serial Taxila property; numerical dates not adopted here.

records.urban_foundation: Bhir probably founded in the sixth century BCE; Sirkap and Sirsukh are later distinct towns.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: A serial archaeological landscape includes Saraikala, Bhir, Sirkap and Sirsukh; the modern town is another civic footprint.
known_hiatuses: Relocation between settlement footprints is explicit; an uninterrupted same-footprint sequence to the present is not supplied.
records.summary: Taxila records successive towns in one valley. Its Neolithic and Bronze Age evidence belongs to Saraikala; Bhir's historic-city date cannot be extended backwards with that separate sequence.
gaps: Acquire Saraikala's dated excavation sequence.
Map the separate ancient towns and modern civic footprint; establish intervals between them.

records.name: Harappa

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living Harappa town and protected archaeological mounds in Punjab; overlapping footprints require a spatial register.
records.evidence_place: Harappa archaeological settlement and overlapping modern town

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: James et al. adopt the site's phase chronology; these are phase bounds, not uncertainty on one founding event.

records.urban_foundation: Kot Diji incipient urbanisation c. 2800–2600 BCE; Mature Harappan urban phase c. 2600–1900 BCE.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: The modern town overlaps part of the ancient settlement; Kenoyer 1991 describes approximately one quarter of the archaeological site under it.
known_hiatuses: A post-1300 BCE gap in the audited evidence is unresolved; this is not a demonstrated abandonment of every part of Harappa.
records.summary: Harappa joins an Indus-period sequence with a modern settlement over part of the mound. The dated sequence reviewed here reaches about 1300 BCE; the intervening history beneath living streets remains the deciding gap.
gaps: No audited occupation series from c. 1300 BCE through Early Historic, medieval and modern periods was obtained.
James et al.'s phrase about continuous occupation does not itself supply that missing dated series.
Bound the area under the modern town and examine accessible construction archives and non-invasive survey.

records.name: Varanasi

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living city in Uttar Pradesh; pin is a broad civic anchor, not Rajghat's trench position.

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: c. 800 BCE at Rajghat in the cited excavation chronology
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: ASI 2012 Introduction reports Period IA; it also suggests a 400–500-year earlier revision, retained as an unresolved chronological assertion.

earlier_regional_evidence.date_label: Second-millennium BCE chronology proposed in ASI introduction
earlier_regional_evidence.relationship: Separate sites or satellite settlements; not imported as a city-wide founding date.

records.urban_foundation: The ASI introduction places urban-metropolis development around the middle of the first millennium BCE.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Rajghat is the northern ancient settlement within the wider modern city; Akatha, Ramnagar and Sarai Mohana are separately located sites.
known_hiatuses: The 1940 excavation did not reach natural soil and some upper strata were damaged by railway works; city-wide continuity remains unproven here.
records.summary: Rajghat anchors ancient Varanasi in excavated deposits. A proposed earlier date around 1300–1200 BCE needs source-specific review, and early neighbouring settlements require their own footprint links.
gaps: Resolve the suggested earlier chronology using the original Rajghat and nearby-site dates.
Assemble occupation evidence connecting the ancient core with the modern city through every intervening period.

chronology_anchors.basis: ASI introduction proposes pushing the c. 800 BCE start back 400–500 years; no sample-level dating audit in this package.

records.name: Ujjain

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: ASI 1957–58 excavation report dates the earliest fortified phase at Garh-Kalika.

records.urban_foundation: Fortified citadel and settlement in Period I, c. 700–500 BCE.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Garh-Kalika mound represents ancient Ujjayini on the northern side of the modern city.
known_hiatuses: No city-wide gap catalogue was obtained; long occupation at a mound does not demonstrate every modern quarter's continuity.
records.summary: Ujjain has an excavated early historic urban sequence. Earlier Chalcolithic settlements in the Malwa region do not extend the city's own demonstrated occupation into the Indus period.
gaps: Join the excavated mound sequence to later inhabited quarters.
Review recent excavation and dating records before adopting an older city foundation.

records.name: Mathura

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.evidence_place: Excavated Mathura city areas, including Ambarish Tila

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: Period I, sixth to closing fourth century BCE
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: ASI 1975–76 report dates the site's Painted Grey Ware horizon; the general PGW culture range is not substituted for this local date.

records.urban_foundation: Growth from the early settlement through Northern Black Polished Ware and later urban phases; exact urban founding event unresolved.

occupation_spans.scope: report's Period I; rounded century bounds

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Several excavation areas lie within the present city; the local horizons have different survival and coverage.
known_hiatuses: No complete same-footprint sequence to the present is supplied by this annual excavation section.
records.summary: Mathura's reviewed excavation report begins with a small settlement in its sixth–fourth-century BCE Period I. Its date comes from that city's sequence, independently of older dates assigned to the wider ceramic culture.
gaps: Audit revised radiocarbon dates and their local contexts.
Join later urban deposits across the separate excavation areas through to the modern city.

records.name: Patna / Pataliputra

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.evidence_place: Four Pataliputra cuttings within Patna City

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: c. sixth century BCE in the reported city cuttings
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: ASI 1955–56 report dates the earliest occupation in four Patna City excavation areas.

records.urban_foundation: First-millennium BCE Pataliputra; no single founding date inferred from the cuttings.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Ancient Pataliputra remains lie under modern Patna; evidence varies among the sampled urban areas.
known_hiatuses: ASI 1955–56 reports a gap of nearly a thousand years, CE 600–1600, in the four excavated areas; extent across the entire city unknown.
records.summary: Patna occupies the Pataliputra area. The annual report records a major CE 600–1600 gap in its sampled sequence, which makes an uninterrupted-city claim require evidence from other parts of the city.
gaps: Map the sampled areas and locate occupation during the reported gap elsewhere in Patna.
Distinguish literary foundation history from excavated settlement onset.

records.name: Rajgir / Rajagriha

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living town in Nalanda district, Bihar.

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: Early Historic pre-rampart horizon; calendar onset unresolved
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: ASI 1962–63 reports Northern Black Polished Ware and an old uncalibrated radiocarbon estimate. No calendar founding date is manufactured.

records.urban_foundation: Historically early capital; the reviewed sample is not a secure date for initial city construction.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Old Rajagriha, new fort and the living town are separate parts of a larger valley settlement landscape.
known_hiatuses: No whole-valley continuity assessment was obtained.
records.summary: Rajgir's retrieved excavation section establishes an Early Historic sequence. Its old radiocarbon result needs recalibration and context review before it can supply a calendar onset or a continuous bridge to the present town.
gaps: Acquire full reports, laboratory sample records and a modern calibrated chronology.
Map Old Rajgir, New Rajgir and present habitation; assess settlement shifts and gaps.

chronology_anchors.basis: Printed with 5730-year half-life; do not read as a calibrated calendar interval.

records.name: Srinagar and Burzahom

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living Srinagar in the Kashmir Valley; the pin identifies the present city, not Burzahom.
records.evidence_place: Present Srinagar urban core; Burzahom recorded separately

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: No Bronze Age onset for the present urban core adopted
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Burzahom is a separately located Neolithic site; Pandrenthan and modern Srinagar have distinct historical footprints.

earlier_regional_evidence.date_label: Neolithic and Megalithic sequence c. 3000–1000 BCE; later Early Historic activity
earlier_regional_evidence.relationship: Separate site in the modern district; contemporaneity is not Harappan cultural affiliation.

records.urban_foundation: Historical traditions associate earlier Srinagari with Pandrenthan; no Bronze Age urban foundation adopted.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Burzahom lies northeast of the modern core. Pandrenthan is another ancient urban locus; none supplies an automatic same-footprint sequence for Srinagar.
known_hiatuses: Burzahom's last activity in the synthesis is third–fourth century CE; subsequent connection to Srinagar remains unjoined.
records.summary: Burzahom demonstrates habitation during the Indus period in the Srinagar region. A dated chain from its Neolithic settlement to the present city was not obtained.
gaps: Obtain the present urban core's earliest securely dated occupation sequence.
Map Burzahom, Pandrenthan and later Srinagar independently before testing a spatial or population connection.

records.name: Rupnagar / Ropar

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living town and district centre in Punjab.

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: Period I c. 2000–1400 BCE in the ASI site card
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Source-reported Harappan-phase bounds; the early chronology needs modern dating review.

records.urban_foundation: Harappan and later occupation at the mound; a single enduring urban foundation is not established.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Protected mound within modern Rupnagar; later building surrounds the archaeological area.
known_hiatuses: Reported post-Period I break, approximately 1400–1000 BCE on the card's dates.
Other listed periods leave CE 600–800 and CE 1000–1300 intervals unfilled in this card; these are evidence gaps, not independently audited city-wide abandonments.
records.summary: Rupnagar supplies a direct Harappan-to-later-period comparison in a living town. The ASI card explicitly records a break after Period I, followed by Painted Grey Ware occupation around 1000–700 BCE.
gaps: Review the 2011–12 excavation and new absolute dates.
Determine whether occupation continued elsewhere during the mound's reported breaks.

records.name: Vadnagar

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.evidence_place: Fortified town and excavation areas, Vadnagar

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Approximate settlement anchor combining the published c. 2754 cal BP statement with the nomination's c. 750 BCE onset; not a sample confidence interval.

records.urban_foundation: Pre-rampart settlement precedes the later fortified town; no Indus-period urban founding date established.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: The living fortified town overlies the excavated mound and retains the old settlement footprint at town scale.
known_hiatuses: The nomination and research abstract report unbroken occupation; this register has not independently audited every intervening boundary.
records.summary: Vadnagar has the clearest published long-continuity claim in this register, with seven cultural stages beneath a living town. The supported onset is early first millennium BCE; a press-reported 1400 BCE lead still needs its primary dating record.
gaps: Acquire the complete dating article and sample table for independent sequence review.
Obtain the proposed older determinations with context, material, calibration and stratigraphic model.

records.name: Lumbini

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Lumbini sacred garden within the present Lumbini Sanskritik municipal area; map pin indexes the sacred place.
records.evidence_place: Maya Devi Temple sacred area, Lumbini

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Primary excavation dating of structures below the Maya Devi Temple.

earlier_regional_evidence.place: Village a few hundred metres south of Maya Devi Temple
earlier_regional_evidence.relationship: Separate village; approximate date meets the younger comparison boundary and is not assigned Harappan affiliation.

records.urban_foundation: Sixth-century BCE timber shrine does not date a city foundation.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: The sacred garden and modern municipal settlement are different spatial units; an older village is a few hundred metres south.
known_hiatuses: The reviewed shrine sequence is not a year-by-year history of residential occupation to the present.
records.summary: Lumbini preserves an early sacred-place sequence. Its nearby c. 1300 BCE village is an older habitation lead at the edge of the Late Harappan comparison interval, with no demonstrated village-to-modern-town bridge.
gaps: Acquire the older village's complete dating and stratigraphic record.
Separate temple use, village habitation and the history of modern Lumbini Sanskritik municipality.

records.name: Tilaurakot / Kapilavastu

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Protected archaeological place in Kapilvastu district beside living settlements; not a continuously occupied modern city demonstrated here.

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: ICOMOS 2025 evaluation describes the earliest excavated timber habitation.

records.urban_foundation: Urban grid and fortification develop from the sixth century BCE.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Archaeological city north of Taulihawa; remains also under modern Shivagarh. The named modern district is not the ancient city footprint.
known_hiatuses: Gradual abandonment of the urban form from first–second century CE; later activity does not supply an uninterrupted civic sequence.
records.summary: Tilaurakot developed from an eighth-century BCE settlement into a sixth-century BCE urban form. The evaluation records gradual abandonment beginning in the first–second century CE and keeps its Kapilavastu identification under assessment.
gaps: Distinguish later temple use from residential continuation.
Establish the dated histories of Shivagarh and Taulihawa independently of the ancient city name.

records.name: Anuradhapura

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Living city and sacred archaeological landscape in North Central Province.

earliest_evidence_bce.basis: Coningham et al. 1996 p. 79 reports this calibrated occupation range for light structures and occupation floors; not uncertainty on the founding of the whole city.

earlier_regional_evidence.place: Broader low mound on left bank of Malwattu Oya
earlier_regional_evidence.date_label: Hunter-gatherer occupation cited as early as c. 4000 BCE
earlier_regional_evidence.relationship: Earlier human presence cited on printed p. 79; source is Deraniyagala 1992 p. 434, not independently acquired here. No dated bridge to Period K established.

records.urban_foundation: Iron Age settlement precedes the later capital; no Indus-period city foundation established.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: The ancient citadel, sacred area and modern city are distinct overlapping and adjacent units.
known_hiatuses: UNESCO describes the capital as abandoned after the 993 CE invasion. Excavation sequences and surviving sacred activity have different spatial and temporal scopes; complete regional depopulation is not inferred.
records.summary: Anuradhapura preserves a long Iron Age-to-medieval sequence and a living sacred landscape. ASW2's early settled horizon dates to 840–460 BCE; reported c. 4000 BCE hunter-gatherer evidence elsewhere on the mound leaves the intervening occupation unresolved.
gaps: Audit the primary basal chronology and any earlier lithics separately from settled occupation.
Trace the inhabited and ritual enclaves through the post-capital period and modern urban growth.

records.name: Mahasthangarh / Mahasthan

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Mahasthan villages and protected citadel in Shibganj, Bogura district; not the foundation date of Bogura municipality.

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: Late fourth–third century BCE urban settlement
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: State Party synthesis and its quoted eastern-rampart stratigraphic table.

earlier_regional_evidence.date_label: Modern city chronology not audited here
earlier_regional_evidence.relationship: Separate nearby city; ancient Mahasthan dates are not transferred to it.

records.urban_foundation: Urban core founded around fourth–third century BCE in the source synthesis.

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

records.spatial_relation: Living villages and ritual places occupy parts of the Mahasthan landscape; modern Bogura city is a separate place to the south.
known_hiatuses: The synthesis describes thirteenth-century damage and later occupation in different parts; upper table phases include broad uncertain intervals.
records.summary: Mahasthan combines an excavated ancient urban core with later habitation and sacred use. Its eastern-rampart table and landscape history support long persistence with changing occupied areas, beginning after the Indus period.
gaps: Obtain Alam and Salles 2001 and later primary stratigraphic reports.
Resolve the spatial extent of occupation after the thirteenth-century damage; date the modern villages separately.

records.name: Dholavira

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Ancient city and separate nearby living village in Kachchh, Gujarat.

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: c. 3000 BCE; source occupation range c. 3000–1500 BCE
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: UNESCO site description's approximate settlement range.

records.urban_foundation: Harappan urban settlement within the c. 3000–1500 BCE site history.

occupation_spans.scope: broad site chronology; no uninterrupted assertion

indus_overlap.basis: Coded only for evidence at the named evidence_place. A nearby site is listed separately. Contemporaneity does not assign Indus cultural affiliation.

known_hiatuses: Ancient city occupation ends around 1500 BCE in the source summary; the later sequence to the modern village is not demonstrated.

Obtain the modern village's own settlement history.

records.name: Mohenjo-daro

coordinate_precision.basis: Project-authored approximate geographic index point, rounded to 0.01 degree; not a surveyed centre or ancient boundary.

records.modern_civic_identity: Archaeological site near modern settlements in Sindh; no living municipality of the ancient city is asserted.

earliest_evidence_bce.date_label: Third millennium BCE; deeper foundation unresolved
earliest_evidence_bce.basis: UNESCO synthesis uses broad and varying third-millennium city dates; no single calendar foundation is adopted.

records.urban_foundation: Mature Indus urban phase c. 2600–1900 BCE; initial settlement depth unresolved.

occupation_spans.scope: broad source-reported third-millennium occupation; last-use boundary unresolved

gaps: Acquire source-specific dates for the latest occupation and deeper foundations.
Keep later monuments, visitors and nearby villages separate from habitation of the Bronze Age city.
